data.kicker: Vector search cheat sheet · 6 index types
title: Same Embeddings.
Different Indexes.
Different Trade-offs.

intro.before: Every vector database answers nearest-neighbour queries, but the index decides

bullets.text: Exact results: perfect recall by definition
No training, no tuning, easy updates
The baseline to measure other indexes
Query cost grows with every vector added
Clusters vectors with k-means, scans a few
nprobe trades speed for recall per query
Simple, and pairs well with compression
Misses neighbours in unprobed clusters
Greedy walk from a sparse top layer down
High recall at low latency; common default
Supports incremental inserts
Graph links cost a lot of extra memory
Splits vectors into chunks, 1-byte code each
Cuts memory sharply: 3 KB → 96 B here
Fast approximate distances via lookup tables
Lossy: re-rank with full vectors
Random hyperplanes hash vectors to buckets
No training; easy to shard and stream
Well-understood probability guarantees
Needs many tables for good recall

items.title: DiskANN
items.tagline: Graph on SSD, codes in RAM

bullets.text: Keeps the graph and full vectors on SSD
Compressed codes in RAM guide the search
Scales past RAM on a single machine
Slower than in-memory graphs; SSD-bound

data.overview_title: Where each index does its work

principles.sub: Benchmark against a flat index; recall@10 and p95 latency beat any default setting.
Reach for compression or disk-based indexes only when memory becomes the limit.
Retrieve extra candidates with PQ codes, then re-score them exactly.

rows.q: Low latency, high recall, RAM ok
